b: Something broke in me last weekend and I'm not sure what to do about it. I'm a M(50) and have been married to my wife F(50) for almost 30 years. We married in our early 20's and she is the only person I have ever been intimate with. To my knowledge, I am her only one as well. I would say for the most part, our marriage has been good. Like all marriages, there have been ups and downs but have made it work balancing work and raising kids.

It seems over the past 5 years, she has become very condescending, criticizing everything I do, criticizing how I look (I never criticize her), and for not doing enough. It doesn't matter how hard I try, I can't seem to do enough to please her. This carried over into the bedroom as well. It was very clinical, requiring numerous steps before beginning. Due to the constant criticisms and fear of being criticized, it affected my performance, which she took personally and only made it worse. We haven't been intimate in years.

Then this past weekend, I arrived home from out of town work. I immediately start helping around the house, cooking dinner, catching up the laundry, fulfilling extra curricular activities for our kids, taking out the trash, you know, just normal things. She had given me a list of things to do and continued to pile on right up until I had to leave for work again.

I couldn't complete all the items before I had to leave and was made to feel like complete trash. This is when I felt something break in my spirit. I am a good man and I try really hard. I have tried to be the best husband and father I could be but this broke me and I have not been the same since. I keep asking myself is this all I have to look forward to for what is left of my life? I don't even want to consider the "D" word because I take the institution of marriage seriously but I feel completely hopeless.

**Edit** After reading through the replies, I wanted to address some of those here rather than reply to each individual reply. I did not come here first. I have tried to discuss my concerns with her multiple times. Yes, she is in perimenopause and is afraid to take HRT due to her own research. She has acknowledged her lack of filter and changes to her personality but has not made an effort to change. I am not a doormat and stand my ground on many things. But, as I mentioned in my OP, I take marriage seriously and have lived out things in our vows like "in sickness and in health" especially the sickness part through some very serious, life threatening events for her. I'm just not willing to quickly throw away 30+ years.
I truly appreciate all of the replies as I came here seeking different perspectives with hopes that other couples experienced similar issues and found ways to work through them.
